citation: Zhang Q, Duan Z, Xiang D, Yu Y, Tian J (2021). The effects of prosocial cartoon examples on children's donating behavior. Psychology Research and Behavior Management 14:1257-1268. doi:10.2147/PRBM.S315068
arm_label: Prosocial (donation) cartoons vs control (Peppa Pig, no donation content) cartoons
treatment_description: Four cartoon episodes depicting donation (e.g. Peppa Pig Father's Donation by Running, Big Head Son and Little Head Father's Charity, Enthusiastic Kiki, Big Ear Tutu's Blood Donation); 15 min/day for 4 consecutive days, watched in classroom groups of about 13.
control_description: Four Peppa Pig episodes with no donation (and no antisocial) content (Talent Day, Perfume, Takes the Train, Fishpond); same schedule.
outcome_description: Posttest donation task: number of 5 teddy-bear dolls (0-5) donated to disadvantaged peers through the China Hope Project; children could keep the rest.
location: Table 4 (Analysis of Variance on Donating Behavior), p. 1263
notes: F is the cartoon main effect in a 2 (cartoon) x 2 (gender) x 3 (age) ANOVA, df (1,144), partial eta2 = 0.28, p < .001; not a simple two-group F. No overall posttest mean/SD by condition is printed; Table 3 (p. 1263) gives M+-SD by condition x gender x age (Total row: prosocial male 4.28+-0.83, female 4.38+-0.78; control male 3.23+-1.39, female 2.79+-1.28; printed N 78 per condition). Pretest (Table 2): prosocial 2.29+-1.30, control 2.56+-1.41; pretest condition t(154) = -1.24, p = .22. Random assignment stated ('Half of them were randomly assigned to watch prosocial cartoons...'). Paper says bears would be sent via China Hope Project but does not report delivery. Posttest given right after the 4th cartoon (after 4 days of exposure). No preregistration mentioned; data at osf.io/ae78r. Source read: Dovepress HTML and PDF (dovepress.com/article/download/67739).

citation: Chen H, Lyu D, Zhu L (2025). The effectiveness of social-themed picture book reading in promoting children's prosocial behavior. Frontiers in Psychology 16:1569925. doi:10.3389/fpsyg.2025.1569925
arm_label: Social-themed picture books (parent-child shared reading) vs matched non-social picture books
treatment_description: Parent-child shared reading of 16 socially themed picture books (cooperation, sharing, helping, friendship), two books per week for 8 weeks, 20-30 min sessions.
control_description: Parent-child shared reading of 16 books on science, creativity and daily habits, matched on length, illustration-to-text ratio and interactive format, without social-emotional content; same schedule.
delay: delayed: posttest after the 8-week reading programme ended; interval since last reading not stated
outcome_description: Sharing task (adapted dictator game): number of 7 chosen stickers placed in envelope for children at another kindergarten; posttest score.
location: Table 3 (Results); columns: intervention pretest, intervention posttest, control pretest, control posttest
notes: Values recorded are POSTTEST; pretest share: intervention 0.50 (1.00), control 0.90 (1.39). Table 3 caption says 'Means and standard errors' but the Descriptive statistics section says 'mean and standard deviation'; values are treated as SDs (SEs of 1.18-1.53 with n = 30 on a 0-7 scale would be implausible). n = 30 per group from the design; per-analysis n not reported. Authors' primary analysis is a group x time RM-ANOVA on TOTAL prosocial behaviour (helping + sharing): interaction F = 4.633, p = 0.036, df = 55, eta2 = 0.077; sharing alone is not tested separately. Total score mixes the pen-dropping helping task (H-type), so it is not recorded as a P outcome. Random assignment of parent-child dyads stated. Whether stickers were actually delivered to the other kindergarten is not stated. Participants section misprints '60 middle school children'. No preregistration statement.

citation: Sakai JT, Chintaluru Y, Raymond KM, McWilliams S, Carter RM, Winters DE, Mikulich-Gilbertson SK (2023). A revised prosocial behavior game: testing associations with psychopathic traits and the effects of moral elevation using a randomized clinical trial. PLOS ONE 18(4):e0283279
arm_label: Moral elevation video (subway rescue) vs control nature video
treatment_description: Moral elevation video depicting a man risking his life to save another in the New York subway, shown between Run 1 and Run 2 of the game.
control_description: Nature video of similar length (series of images of the ocean, green spaces and forests).
outcome_description: AlAn's Short Game v.2, Run 2 vs Run 1: number of prosocial decisions (Active Type A trials rejected, where self gains and Red Cross loses, plus Active Type B trials accepted, where self loses and Red Cross gains).
quote: The Group by Run interaction was non-significant (F1, 478 = 2.40; p = 0.122).
location: Results, 'Testing the effects of moral elevation on game behavior'; group ns from Fig 4 caption
notes: F is the Group x Run interaction from a mixed-model ANCOVA adjusted for age, race and Red Cross visual analog scale (pre- vs post-video change by group); Group main effect F(1,478) = 0.42, p = 0.52. Means/SDs by group and run not reported in text (Fig 4 plots adjusted estimates). Analysed mITT n = 485 (237 elevation, 248 control). Randomization: within-sex permuted blocks in REDCap. Payment: '$20 plus earnings from playing'; whether Red Cross allocations were actually donated is not stated. Recipient is a charity (Red Cross); choices not shared with others. Methods and Results label Group 1/2 inconsistently. No outcome explicitly labelled primary; this is the hypothesis test. Treatment is a real-event video, coded modern_invented (not traditional). Registered at ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03834467.

citation: Horton JJ, Rand DG, Zeckhauser RJ (2011). The online laboratory: conducting experiments in a real labor market. Experimental Economics 14:399-425 (arXiv:1004.2931), religious priming replication
arm_label: Religious passage (Mark 10:17-23, charity) vs neutral passage (three fish species)
country: Online MTurk workers (US and non-US; composition not reported)
treatment_description: Read a Christian religious passage about the importance of charity (Mark 10:17-23) before the PD.
control_description: Read a passage of equal length describing three species of fish.
outcome_description: One-shot prisoner's dilemma cooperation (1 = cooperate) with a randomly matched worker; payoffs 120/120, 40/160, 160/40, 80/80 cents paid for real.

values.other: Logistic regression with robust SEs (prime, believer, prime x believer, gender, age, country, religion): main effect of prime p = 0.169, coefficient and SE not reported; prime x believer coeff = 2.15, p = 0.001. Cooperation rates by condition shown only in Figure 1 (image, not readable through the tool). n_t = 90, n_c = 99.

quote: we found no significant main effect of prime (p=0.169)
location: arXiv:1004.2931, Section 3.4 'Replication: Priming' (no page numbers in version read); Figure 1
notes: Ns from: 'Subjects were randomly assigned to either the religious prime group (N = 90) or a neutral prime group (N = 99).' Prime effect is reported only conditional on covariates and the interaction term, so p = 0.169 is not a simple two-group test. Figure 1 caption: prime increases cooperation among believers but not non-believers; believer = ever had an experience convincing them God exists. Read the arXiv version, not the published Experimental Economics version. weird left null: mixed US/non-US sample. Real payments: 'individualized payments based on their choices and the choices of other workers ... matched retroactively'.
